AlmostPeriodicity.LProp.statement: Let $G$ be a finite additive commutative group equipped with a measurable space structure. Let $k, m \in \mathbb{N}$ be natural numbers, $\varepsilon \in \mathbb{R}$ a real number, $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ a function and $A \subseteq G$ a finite set. For a $k$-tuple $a = (a_i)_{i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,k}$ of elements of $G$, $\mathrm{LProp}(k,m,\varepsilon,f,A,a)$ is the proposition the inequality $\Big\| x \mapsto \sum_{i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,k} f(x - a_i) - k\,(\mu_A \ast_d f)(x) \Big\|_{[2m]} \le k\,\varepsilon\,\|f\|_{[2m]}$. Here, for $p \in [0,\infty]$ and $h : G \to \mathbb{C}$, $\|h\|_{[p]}$ denotes $\mathrm{dLpNorm}(p, h)$, the $L^p$ norm of $h$ with respect to the counting measure on $G$ (so for $0<p<\infty$, $\|h\|_{[p]} = (\sum_{x \in G} |h(x)|^p)^{1/p}$); $\mu_A : G \to \mathbb{C}$ is the normalised indicator $\mu_A = |A|^{-1}\mathbf{1}_A$ (with $|A|^{-1}$ taken as $0$ when $A$ is empty); and $(u \ast_d v)(y) = \sum_{(x_1,x_2) \in G\times G,\ x_1 + x_2 = y} u(x_1)v(x_2)$ is the convolution of $u, v : G \to \mathbb{C}$.

AlmostPeriodicity.l.statement: Let $G$ be a finite additive commutative group equipped with a measurable space structure. Let $k, m \in \mathbb{N}$ be natural numbers, $\varepsilon \in \mathbb{R}$ a real number, $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ a function and $A \subseteq G$ a finite set. $l(k,m,\varepsilon,f,A)$ is the finite set of all $k$-tuples $a = (a_i)_{i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,k} \in A^k$ (i.e. $a : \mathrm{Fin}\,k \to G$ with every $a_i \in A$) such that $\mathrm{LProp}(k,m,\varepsilon,f,A,a)$ holds, namely the inequality $\Big\| x \mapsto \sum_{i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,k} f(x - a_i) - k\,(\mu_A \ast_d f)(x) \Big\|_{[2m]} \le k\,\varepsilon\,\|f\|_{[2m]}$. Here, for $p \in [0,\infty]$ and $h : G \to \mathbb{C}$, $\|h\|_{[p]}$ denotes $\mathrm{dLpNorm}(p, h)$, the $L^p$ norm of $h$ with respect to the counting measure on $G$ (so for $0<p<\infty$, $\|h\|_{[p]} = (\sum_{x \in G} |h(x)|^p)^{1/p}$); $\mu_A : G \to \mathbb{C}$ is the normalised indicator $\mu_A = |A|^{-1}\mathbf{1}_A$ (with $|A|^{-1}$ taken as $0$ when $A$ is empty); and $(u \ast_d v)(y) = \sum_{(x_1,x_2) \in G\times G,\ x_1 + x_2 = y} u(x_1)v(x_2)$ is the convolution of $u, v : G \to \mathbb{C}$.
